The “Oracle” of Omaha pointed to Berkshire, saying the company’s value declined by half on three separate occasions despite no underlying business problem.

He identified borrowing and emotional decision-making as greater dangers than temporary market declines. "If you can’t handle it psychologically, then you really shouldn’t own stocks, because you’re going to buy and sell them at the wrong time," he said.

Buffett also said that investors should trust their own understanding and judgment rather than relying on others to tell them what to do. “If you don’t understand it yourself you’re going to be affected by the next person you talk to,” he said.
The investor also said he could not determine whether one day represented an ideal buying opportunity, but emphasized that investing should be evaluated over 20- or 30-year periods.
